Instructions to Candidates
  • This university examination consists of two 60-minute sections totaling 36 questions (36 marks).
  • Part A (Questions 1–18) covers first-order separable/linear/exact ODEs, second-order linear homogeneous ODEs, Wronskian, undetermined coefficients, and variation of parameters.
  • Part B (Questions 19–36) covers Laplace transforms, Dirac delta/step forcing, linear systems & phase planes, power series/Frobenius, and RK4 numerical methods.

1 Systems of Linear ODEs Foundational [1 mark]
The matrix of x′=Ax\mathbf x'=A\mathbf xx′=Ax has eigenvalues -3 and 2. The origin is a:
A. center (stable, not asymptotically)
B. unstable node
C. stable spiral
D. saddle point (unstable)
Correct Answer: (D) — saddle point (unstable)
Real eigenvalues of opposite sign give a saddle; same sign gives a node (stable if negative). Here: saddle point (unstable).

13 Nonhomogeneous Equations, Undetermined Coefficients & Resonance Standard [1 mark]
Consider the nonhomogeneous second-order linear differential equation y′′−5y′+6y=12x+8y'' - 5y' + 6y = 12x + 8y′′−5y′+6y=12x+8. yh(x)=c1e2x+c2e3xy_h(x) = c_1e^{2x} + c_2e^{3x}yh​(x)=c1​e2x+c2​e3x is the general solution to the corresponding homogeneous equation. Find the particular solution yp(x)y_p(x)yp​(x) using the method of undetermined coefficients, and then determine the value of the constant AAA such that yp(x)=Ax+By_p(x) = Ax + Byp​(x)=Ax+B for some constant BBB.
A. A=2A = 2A=2
B. A=6A = 6A=6
C. A=12A = 12A=12
D. A=3A = 3A=3
Correct Answer: (A) — A=2A = 2A=2
The given nonhomogeneous differential equation is y′′−5y′+6y=12x+8y'' - 5y' + 6y = 12x + 8y′′−5y′+6y=12x+8. \nThe form of the nonhomogeneous term is g(x)=12x+8g(x) = 12x + 8g(x)=12x+8, which is a polynomial of degree 1. Thus, we assume a particular solution of the form yp(x)=Ax+By_p(x) = Ax + Byp​(x)=Ax+B.

We need to find the first and second derivatives of yp(x)y_p(x)yp​(x):
yp′(x)=Ay_p'(x) = Ayp′​(x)=A
yp′′(x)=0y_p''(x) = 0yp′′​(x)=0

Substitute these into the differential equation:
0−5(A)+6(Ax+B)=12x+80 - 5(A) + 6(Ax + B) = 12x + 80−5(A)+6(Ax+B)=12x+8
−5A+6Ax+6B=12x+8-5A + 6Ax + 6B = 12x + 8−5A+6Ax+6B=12x+8
6Ax+(6B−5A)=12x+86Ax + (6B - 5A) = 12x + 86Ax+(6B−5A)=12x+8

Equating the coefficients of like powers of xxx:
For the xxx term: 6A=126A = 126A=12 ⇒\Rightarrow⇒ A=2A = 2A=2.
For the constant term: 6B−5A=86B - 5A = 86B−5A=8.
Substitute A=2A = 2A=2 into the second equation:
6B−5(2)=86B - 5(2) = 86B−5(2)=8
6B−10=86B - 10 = 86B−10=8
6B=186B = 186B=18
B=3B = 3B=3

Therefore, the particular solution is yp(x)=2x+3y_p(x) = 2x + 3yp​(x)=2x+3. The value of the constant AAA is 2.

18 Linear First-Order Equations, Integrating Factors & Nonlinear Reductions Challenging [1 mark]
Consider the first-order linear differential equation dydx+P(x)y=Q(x)\frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x)dxdy​+P(x)y=Q(x). If the integrating factor for this equation is given by ex2e^{x^2}ex2 and Q(x)=2xex2Q(x) = 2xe^{x^2}Q(x)=2xex2, find the value of the constant CCC in the general solution if y(0)=3y(0) = 3y(0)=3. The general solution is of the form y=e−x2(∫Q(x)e−x2dx+C)y = e^{-x^2} \left( \int Q(x) e^{-x^2} dx + C \right)y=e−x2(∫Q(x)e−x2dx+C).
A. 444
B. 333
C. 666
D. 111
Correct Answer: (B) — 333
The given differential equation is in the form dydx+P(x)y=Q(x)\frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x)dxdy​+P(x)y=Q(x). The integrating factor (IF) is given by e∫P(x)dxe^{\int P(x) dx}e∫P(x)dx. We are told that the integrating factor is ex2e^{x^2}ex2. Therefore, ∫P(x)dx=x2\int P(x) dx = x^2∫P(x)dx=x2, which implies P(x)=2xP(x) = 2xP(x)=2x.

The general solution to a first-order linear differential equation is given by y⋅IF=∫Q(x)⋅IF dx+Cy \cdot \text{IF} = \int Q(x) \cdot \text{IF} \, dx + Cy⋅IF=∫Q(x)⋅IFdx+C.
Substituting the IF and Q(x)Q(x)Q(x), we get:
yex2=∫(2xex2)e−x2 dx+Cy e^{x^2} = \int (2xe^{x^2}) e^{-x^2} \, dx + Cyex2=∫(2xex2)e−x2dx+C
yex2=∫2x dx+Cy e^{x^2} = \int 2x \, dx + Cyex2=∫2xdx+C
yex2=x2+Cy e^{x^2} = x^2 + Cyex2=x2+C
Now, we need to find the value of CCC using the initial condition y(0)=3y(0) = 3y(0)=3.
Substitute x=0x=0x=0 and y=3y=3y=3 into the general solution:
3e02=02+C3 e^{0^2} = 0^2 + C3e02=02+C
3⋅1=0+C3 \cdot 1 = 0 + C3⋅1=0+C
C=3C = 3C=3.
Therefore, the value of the constant CCC is 3.
